title: Reconocimiento y patrimonio: 'gozar de protección' y 'ser declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad'

sections.content: Beyond co-official languages, several Statutes of Autonomy and national laws grant legal protection and promotion ('gozan de protección y promoción') to specific linguistic modalities ('modalidades lingüísticas') and communicative systems. These include **el bable o asturiano** in the Principality of Asturias, **el aragonés** in Aragon, **el leonés** in Castile and León, the officially recognized **Lengua de Signos Española (LSE)** and **Lengua de Signos Catalana (LSC)** (Law 27/2007), and **el silbo gomero**, an ancient whistled language on the Canary Island of La Gomera declared Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO.

items.spanish: El bable o asturiano goza de protección y difusión en el Principado de Asturias.
items.english: Bable or Asturian enjoys protection and promotion in the Principality of Asturias.

items.spanish: El silbo gomero fue declarado Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad por la UNESCO.
items.english: The Silbo Gomero was declared Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO.

items.spanish: La ley española reconoce oficialmente la Lengua de Signos Española y la Lengua de Signos Catalana.
items.english: Spanish law officially recognizes Spanish Sign Language and Catalan Sign Language.

sections.content: Remember **el silbo gomero** (from the island of **La Gomera**, in the Canary Islands): a whistled language capable of transmitting messages in Spanish across deep ravines ('barrancos'), recognized by UNESCO.
